daas-irab:33-35.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أُولُوا﴾ khabar (predicate), nominative by the wāw because it is treated like the sound masculine plural. ﴿قُوَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَأُولُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أولو. ﴿بَأْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَدِيدٍ﴾ an adjective (naʿt); the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَالْأَمْرُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial and الأمر is mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَيْكِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿فَانْظُرِي﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), and an imperative indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿ماذا﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of انظري; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of an implied condition. ﴿تَأْمُرِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause stands in place of the object of انظري. [Translator's note: so in the source, «والواو فاعل»; in تَأْمُرِينَ the fāʿil is the yāʾ of the feminine addressee.] ﴿قالَتْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ﴾ inna and its noun; the clause is the object of the speech. ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial and conditional. ﴿دَخَلُوا﴾ the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَرْيَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi of دخلوا. ﴿أَفْسَدُوها﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا. ﴿وَجَعَلُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined to the clause أفسدوها. ﴿أَعِزَّةَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَهْلِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَذِلَّةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to something omitted, an adjective of an implied mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ﴾ both are attached to مرسلة. ﴿فَناظِرَةٌ﴾ conjoined to مرسلة. ﴿بِمَ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun; the two are attached to the verb after them. ﴿يَرْجِعُ الْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾ the clause stands in place of the two objects of ناظرة.

daas-irab:36-38.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; لمّا is adverbial and conditional. ﴿جاءَ سُلَيْمانَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and سليمان is its object; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿أَتُمِدُّونَنِ﴾ the hamza is interrogative, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِمالٍ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تمدونني. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction and ما is a relative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿آتانِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, its object placed first and its fāʿil placed later; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ما; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿مِمَّا﴾ attached to خير. ﴿آتاكُمْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِهَدِيَّتِكُمْ﴾ attached to تفرحون. ﴿تَفْرَحُونَ﴾ the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿ارْجِعْ﴾ an imperative whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ attached to ارجع. ﴿فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; the imperfect verb is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, its fāʿil is latent and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِجُنُودٍ﴾ attached to نأتينهم. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿قِبَلَ﴾ its noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ attached to the khabar. ﴿بِها﴾ attached to قبل; the clause is an adjective (naʿt) of جنود. ﴿وَلَنُخْرِجَنَّهُمْ﴾ conjoined to لنأتينهم. ﴿مِنْها﴾ attached to نخرجنهم. ﴿أَذِلَّةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُمْ صاغِرُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ a vocative; the clause is the object of the speech. ﴿الْمَلَؤُا﴾ a badal (substitute). ﴿أَيُّكُمْ﴾ أي is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَأْتِينِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar. ﴿بِعَرْشِها﴾ attached to يأتيني. ﴿قَبْلَ﴾ an adverb attached to the verb. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an accusative-governing particle. ﴿يَأْتُونِي﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is for protection, and its fāʿil and its object; أن and what follows it, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), are in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ ḥāl.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَكِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾: ﴿وكتابٍ مُبين﴾ is genitive; He means: and the verses of a clear Book. Had it been read ﴿وكتابٌ مبينٌ﴾, by referring it back to "the verses" [i.e. in the nominative], He would mean: and that is a clear Book. And if it were accusative as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ) — as one says: "I passed by a handsome man, and a tall, strapping one (wa-ṭawīlan sharmaḥan)" — that is a valid way. Praise is like his saying:
إلى الملِك القَرْم وابنِ الهُمَام * وليْثَ الكَتيِبة فى المزدَحَمْ
(To the king, the chief, son of the valiant lord — and the lion of the squadron in the press of battle.)
In praise, both its definite and its indefinite are put in the accusative.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿هُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ﴾ is nominative, and if you wish you may put it in the accusative. The accusative is by severance (ʿalā al-qaṭʿ, i.e. as a ḥāl), and the nominative is by a new beginning (istiʾnāf). Similar to it in al-Baqara: ﴿هُدًى للمتَّقِين﴾; and in Luqmān: ﴿هُدىً ورَحْمَةً لِلمُحْسِنِين﴾ is like it.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ﴾: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash put tanwīn on al-shihāb and al-qabas, and the people of Medina made it a genitive construct: (بشهابِ قَبَسٍ). This is like His saying ﴿وَلَدَارُ الآخِرَةِ﴾: of the kind in which a thing is annexed to its own name when its names differ.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿نُودِيَ أَن بُورِكَ مَن فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾: You make (أَنْ) in the position of the accusative if you take the name of Mūsā as latent in ﴿نُودى﴾; and if you do not take the name of Mūsā as latent, (أن) is in the position of the nominative: "that was called out". In the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy: (أَنْ بُورِكتِ النارُ) ("that the fire has been blessed"). ﴿وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾ means the angels. The Arabs say: bārakaka Allāh, bāraka fīka and bāraka ʿalayka (may Allah bless you).

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ﴾: this hāʾ is the hāʾ of ʿimād (the support pronoun, i.e. the pronoun of the matter). It is a noun that does not appear [as a referent]. It has already been explained.

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ﴾: al-jānn is the snake that is neither large nor small. His saying: ﴿وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِراً وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾: he did not turn round.
His saying: ﴿إِنِّي لاَ يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾; then He made an exception, saying: ﴿إَلاَّ مَن ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْناً بَعْدَ سُوۤءٍ﴾ — so this one is forgiven. Someone may say: how was he made one who fears? I say: there are two views on this. One is that you say: the messengers are protected (maʿṣūma), forgiven and safe on the Day of Resurrection, while whoever has mixed a righteous deed with another evil one fears and hopes; that is one view. The other is that you make the exception from those left out of the statement, because the meaning is: the messengers do not fear; fear is only for others than them.
Then He made the exception, saying: except whoever did wrong — for this one does not fear. He means: he was an idolater, then repented and did good, so that one is forgiven, not fearful.
Some grammarians have said that (إلا) in the language is equivalent to wāw (and), and that the meaning of this verse is: the messengers do not fear in My presence, nor does whoever did wrong and then substituted good. They made similar to it the saying of Allah: ﴿لِئَلاّ يَكُونَ لِلناسِ عَلَيْكمْ حُجَّةٌ إلاّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾, i.e. "nor those who did wrong". I have not found that Arabic tolerates what they said, because I do not allow "The people stood except ʿAbd Allāh" while he is standing; exception is only that the noun after illā is taken out of the meaning of the nouns before illā. I do consider it permissible to say "You owe a thousand besides (siwā) another thousand"; if you put (إلاّ) in this position it is sound, and (إلاّ) then has the interpretation they gave. But [illā] on its own [135/b], where a small part is excepted from a large whole — no. Rather, what is like it is that which comes in the meaning of illā, like the meaning of the wāw, without being it [Translator's note: the source has «الولو», evidently for «الواو»].
His saying: ﴿خَالِدِين فِيهَا ما دَامَتِ السَّموَاتُ والأرْضُ إلاّ مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ﴾: in meaning it is "except (i.e. besides) what your Lord wills of increase". So do not make illā equivalent to the wāw, but equivalent to siwā (besides). When siwā is in the position of illā, it is sound in the meaning of the wāw, because you say "I have much wealth besides this", i.e. and this too I have — as though you said: I have much wealth, and this. It is more effective with siwā than with illā, because you may say "I have besides this (siwā hādhā)", but you do not say "illā hādhā".

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿واضْمُم يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوۤءٍ فِي تِسْعِ آيَاتٍ﴾: its meaning is: do this, and it is a sign among nine. Then He said ﴿إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ and did not say "sent" or "dispatched", because his affair is known: that he was sent to Pharaoh. The poet said:
رأتنى بحبليها فصَدَّت مخافةً * وفى الحبل رَوْعاء الفؤاد فَرُوق
(She saw me with her two ropes and shied away in fear; and on the rope was a skittish-hearted, timid one.)
He meant: she saw me coming with her two ropes — with the two ropes of the she-camel — so he left a verb implied, as though he said: she saw me approaching.
His saying ﴿وَإلَى ثَمودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالحاً﴾: accusative by an implied ﴿أرسلنا﴾ (We sent).

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَحَدُواْ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْماً وَعُلُوّاً﴾: he says: they denied the nine signs after their souls had become certain that they were from Allah, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ظلماً عُليّاً), like His saying ﴿وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الكِبَر عُتيّاً﴾ and ﴿عِتِيّا﴾.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَانُ دَاوُودَ﴾: Dāwūd had — according to what they mention — nineteen male children; Sulaymān was singled out for the inheritance only because it was the inheritance of kingship.
His saying ﴿عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيْرِ﴾: the meaning of the speech of the birds; He made it like a man's speech since it was understood. The poet said:
عجبت لَهَا أنَّى يكُون غِناؤها * رَفيعاً ولم تَفتح بمنطقهَا فما
(I marvelled at her: how could her singing be so lofty, when she did not open a mouth for her speech?)
The poet made it like speech since he took it that she was weeping.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَحُشِرَ لِسْلَيْمَانَ جُنُودُهُ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنْس وَٱلطَّيْرِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾: these kinds used to be with Sulaymān when he rode out. ﴿فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾: the first of them were held back for the last of them until they gathered together. It is from wazaʿtu al-rajul (I restrained the man); you say: "I shall surely restrain you (la-azaʿannakum) from wrongdoing", and this is from that.

farraa:19-19.t: As for His saying: ﴿أَوْزِعْنِيۤ﴾, its meaning is: inspire me.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ﴾: the people read it with ḍamma [makutha], and ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa: fa-makatha. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (فتمكَّث). The meaning of ﴿غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ﴾ is: not long in staying; "distant" and "long" are close [in meaning].
His saying ﴿فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ وَجِئْتُكَ﴾: some of the Arabs said aḥaṭṭu, putting the ṭāʾ in place of the tāʾ. When ṭāʾ meets tāʾ and the ṭāʾ before it is vowelless, the Arabs turn the ṭāʾ into tāʾ and say aḥattu, just as they turn the ẓāʾ into tāʾ in His saying ﴿أَوَعَتَّ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنَ الواعِظِينَ﴾, and the dhāl and the dāl into tāʾ, as in ﴿أَخَتُّمْ﴾ — I saw it in some of the copies of ʿAbd Allāh as (وأَخَتُّمْ). And some of the Arabs turn the tāʾ, when it comes after the ṭāʾ, into ṭāʾ and say: aḥaṭṭ.
His saying ﴿وجئْتُكَ مِنْ سبَأ بِنَبإٍ يَقِينٍ﴾: the readers treat ﴿سَبأ﴾ as fully declinable (ijrāʾ), because — according to what they mention — it is a man; likewise make it declinable if it is the name of a mountain. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ did not make it declinable. Al-Ruʾāsī claimed he asked Abū ʿAmr about it and he said: I do not know what it is. He took a [reasonable] position, since he did not know what it was, because when the Arabs name [something] with an unknown name they leave it undeclined, as al-Aʿshā said:
وتدفنُ منه الصَّالحاتُ وإن يُسئْ * يكن ما أساء النارَ فى رأس كَبْكَبا
(His good deeds are buried, while if he does ill, his ill becomes a fire on the top of Kabkab.)
[136/a] It is as though he did not know Kabkab. I heard Abū al-Saffāḥ al-Salūlī say: "This is Abū Ṣuʿrūr, he has come," and he did not decline it, because it is not in their custom of naming.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-ṣuʿrūr is something like gum.
The poet said, not declining it:
الواردون وتيم فى ذُرَا سَبَأٍ * قد عضّ أعْنَاقَهم جلدُ الجواميسِ
(Those who come down to water, and Taym, in the heights of Sabaʾ — the hide of buffaloes has bitten into their necks.)
[Translator's note: in the verse as given here سَبَأٍ carries tanwīn, though it is cited for non-declension.] And if you made it the name of the tribe, if it is a man, or the name of what is around it, if it is a mountain, you would not make it declinable either.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُواْ للَّهِ﴾: It is read ﴿أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُواْ﴾, with ﴿يَسجْدوا﴾ in the position of the accusative; so Ḥamza read it. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan and Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read it without doubling: (ألاَ يَسْجُدُوا), in the sense of "Lo! O you, prostrate!": "you" (hāʾulāʾ) is implied, and (يا) alone suffices for it. He said: I heard some of the Arabs say: "alā yā irḥamānā, alā yā taṣaddaqā ʿalaynā" (Lo! O, have mercy on us both; Lo! O, give alms to us both). He said: he meant me and my companion. The poet — al-Akhṭal — said:
أَلاَ يا اسلمى يا هند هندَ بنى بَدْر * وإن كان حَيَّاناَ عِدىً آخِر الدهر
(Lo! O be safe, O Hind, Hind of Banū Badr, even if our two clans are enemies to the end of time.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: one of the shaykhs — namely al-Kisāʾī — related to me from ʿĪsā al-Hamdānī, who said: I never heard the shaykhs read it except without doubling, intending the imperative. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (هَلاّ تسجدونَ لله) with tāʾ, and this is evidence for whoever reads it without doubling. In the reading of Ubayy: (أَلاَ تسجدونَ لله الذى يعلم سِرَّكم ومَا تَعلِنُون), and that is the proper sense of the passage, because it is a prostration [verse]. Whoever reads ﴿أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُوا﴾ with doubling, it ought not to be a prostration [verse], because the meaning is: Satan made it fair-seeming to them that they should not prostrate; and Allah knows best about that.
His saying ﴿يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ﴾ is with hamza. It is the unseen: the unseen of the heavens and the unseen of the earth. It is also said: it is the water that comes down from the sky and the vegetation from the earth. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (يخرج الخَبْءَ منَ السَّواتِ) [Translator's note: so in the source, for السموات]. (فى) is sound in place of (من) because you say "I shall surely extract from you the knowledge that is in you", and then you omit whichever of the two you wish — I mean (من) and (فى) — and the meaning remains as it is.

farraa:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنْظُرْ﴾: Someone may say: how did he order it to turn away from them, when he said ﴿فانْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾? That is clear in Arabic: he urged it on, saying: "Go with this letter of mine and hurry"; then ﴿فانظر ماذا يَرجعونَ﴾ was placed later, while its meaning is placed earlier. It is also said that he ordered the hoopoe to drop the letter and then hide from her, and it did so: it dropped the letter and flew to an opening in the wall of her council chamber. Allah knows best what is correct in that.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أُلْقِيَ إِلَيَّ كِتَابٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾: she called it noble because it was sealed; so I was told. It is also said: she described the letter as noble to her people because she saw the letter of a king with her, so she called it noble for the nobility of its sender. It is also said that she said (كريم) before she knew that it was from Sulaymān. That does not please me, because she was literate and had read the letter before going out to her council.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ﴾: both are with kasra, I mean inna and inna. Had both been with fatḥa it would be permissible, according to your saying: "it was cast to me that it is from Sulaymān and that it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Their position is then nominative, by repetition (takrīr, i.e. substitution) for "the letter": "it was cast to me that it is from Sulaymān". And if you wish, they are in the position of the accusative because of the dropping of the preposition from them. In the reading of Ubayy: (وأَنْ بِسمِ الله الرحمن الرحيم), and that is evidence for whoever reads both with fatḥa, because (أَن), when its alif is with fatḥa with a verb or with what is quoted, can only be with the nūn lightened.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ تَعْلُواْ﴾: its alif is with fatḥa; kasra is not permissible. It is in the position of the nominative if you make it a repetition on ﴿أُلْقِى﴾, and accusative on [the sense]: "the letter was cast to me with this (bi-dhā)", and then you dropped the bāʾ and put it in the accusative. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وإنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم), and this indicates the kasra, because it is conjoined to: "Indeed, it was cast to me", "and indeed it is from Sulaymān". In the reading of Ubayy, it may be that you make the (أَن) that is in "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate" the same (أن) as in His saying ﴿أن لا تعلوا عَلىَّ﴾, as though in meaning: "it was cast to me: that you not exalt yourselves against me". When it was placed in (بسمِ الله), it was repeated in its position in ﴿أن لا تعلوا﴾, just as Allah said: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنّكُمْ إذا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَاباً وعِظَاماً أَنَّكُمْ﴾ — "annakum" is repeated and its meaning is one, and Allah knows best. Do you not see that the meaning is: does he promise you that you will be brought out when you have become dust and bones?

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلأُ أَفْتُونِي﴾: she made consultation a fatwā (legal opinion). That is permissible because of the breadth of Arabic.
His saying ﴿مَا كُنتُ قَاطِعَةً أَمْراً﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ما كنتُ قاضيةً أمراً), and the meaning is the same. You say: I do not decide (lā aqṭaʿu) a matter without you, and I do not settle (lā aqḍī) a matter without you.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَتْ إِنَّ ٱلْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُواْ قَرْيَةً﴾ is an answer to their saying ﴿نَحْنُ أُولُو قُوَّةٍ وأولُو بأسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾. She said: if they enter your land they will humiliate you, though you are kings. And Allah said: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾: the alif is dropped from His saying (بم) because it means "with what thing will the envoys return?" When (مَا) is in the position of (أىّ, which?) and is then joined to a preposition that governs the genitive, the alif of (مَا) is dropped so that the interrogative is distinguished from the statement. Of this kind is His saying ﴿فِيمَ كُنْتم﴾ and ﴿عَمَّ يتساءَلُونَ﴾; and if you write it in full, that is correct. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
إنا قتلنا بقتلانا سَرَاتكم * أهلَ اللوَاء ففيما يكثر القِيلُ
(We have killed your chiefs, the bearers of the banner, for our slain; so over what is there so much talk?)
And al-Mufaḍḍal also recited to me:
على ما قام يشتمنَا لَئِيمٌ * كخنزير تمرَّغ فى رمَادِ
(Over what does a base man stand up to revile us, like a pig rolling in ashes?)
His saying: ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ﴾ — she means Sulaymān — is like His saying ﴿عَلَى خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهمْ﴾. And she said ﴿بِمَ يَرْجِعُ المُرْسَلُونَ﴾, while her envoy — according to what they mention — was a single woman; she used the plural while it was only one envoy. That is why He said ﴿فلمَّا جَاءَ سُلَيْمانَ﴾, meaning: when the envoy came to Sulaymān. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (فلما جَاءوا سليمان); since He said ﴿المرسَلونَ﴾, ﴿جَاءوا﴾ is sound [too], though the one sent was one. This is indicated by Sulaymān's saying ﴿ارْجِعْ إليْهِمْ﴾.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is with two nūns and a written yāʾ. Ḥamza read it (أَتُمِدُّونَّى بمالٍ): he means the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, but he assimilated the nūn into the nūn and doubled it. ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd read (أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بمالٍ) with two nūns without yāʾ. All are correct.
His saying: ﴿فَمَآ آتَانِيَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ — and he did not say ﴿فما آتانِىَ الله﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the contrast intended is evidently between the yāʾ-less written form آتانِ and the form with the yāʾ] — because it is written without the yāʾ in the text (al-kitāb). Whoever is among those who allow adding to the Quran the yāʾs and wāws that are dropped — as in His saying ﴿وَيَدْعُ الإنْسَان بالشَّرِّ﴾, where he writes in the wāw though it is not in the muṣḥaf, or [reads] al-munādī for al-munād — may say ﴿أتمدُّونَنِ﴾ with the yāʾ, and may vowel it [137/a] with the accusative fatḥa, as was said ﴿وَمَالِىَ لاَ أَعْبُدُ﴾; likewise ﴿فَمَا آتانِىَ الله﴾ is permissible. But I do not care for that, nor do I adopt it. Following the muṣḥaf, when I find a way for it in the speech of the Arabs and the reading of the readers, is dearer to me than departing from it. Abū ʿAmr used to read (إنَّ هَذَيْنِ لسَاحِرَان), and I do not dare to do that; and he read ﴿فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُونَ﴾, adding a wāw to the text, and I do not favour that.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ قِبَلَ لَهُمْ بِهَا﴾: in the muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh it is (لَهُمْ بهم), and it is the same.
His saying: ﴿ٱرْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾: this is from Sulaymān's words to her envoy — he means [the envoy of] Bilqīs. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ارجعوا إليهم), and that is correct, according to what I explained to you about His saying ﴿يأيُّها النَّبىّ إذا طلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ﴾: addressing one person while meaning those with him, which occurs in much speech.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿عِفْرِيتٌ مِّن ٱلْجِنِّ أَنَاْ آتِيكَ بِهِ﴾: al-ʿifrīt is the strong and effective one. Some of the Arabs say ʿifriya for ʿifrīt. Whoever says ʿifriya says in its plural ʿafārin; and whoever says ʿifrīt says ʿafārīt, and he may also say ʿafārin. In one of the two readings: (وَما أُهِلَّ بِهِ للطواغِى), meaning the plural of ṭāghūt. His saying ﴿أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقُومَ مِنْ مَقَامِكَ﴾ means: before he rises from the seat of judgement; he used to sit until midday. He said: I want [something] quicker (than that).

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ ٱلَّذِي عِندَهُ عِلْمٌ مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ أَنَاْ آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ﴾: he says: before the thing reaches you from the extent of your sight. Ibn ʿAbbās said about His saying (عِنْدهُ عِلْمٌ مِنَ الكتاب): ﴿يا حَىُّ يا قيُّوم﴾ ("O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting"). It is mentioned that her throne sank into the ground in its place and then sprang up at Sulaymān's seat.

farraa:41-41.t: As for His saying: ﴿نَكِّرُواْ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا﴾: he ordered them to enlarge it, in order to test her intelligence when she came. The devils had feared that Sulaymān would marry her, so they said: there is something [wrong] in her mind, and her leg is like the leg of a donkey. So Sulaymān ordered the throne to be changed for that reason, and ordered water, which was made to run beneath the glass pavilion (al-ṣarḥ), with fish in it. When she came, it was said to her: (أَهَكَذَا عَرْشُكِ). She recognised it and did not recognise it; she did not say "It is it", nor "It is not it", but said (كَأنَّه هُوَ). Then she lifted her garment from her shins, thinking she was walking into a lujja — a lujja is a great body of water — and he looked upon the most beautiful shins and feet. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وَكَشَفَ عَنْ رِجْليهَا) ("and she uncovered her feet").

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ﴾: he says: she was intelligent; what kept her from the worship of Allah was only the worship of the sun and the moon, which was a custom of her forefathers' religion. The meaning of the passage: what she used to worship — i.e. her worship of the sun and moon — kept her from worshipping Allah. (ما) is in the position of the nominative. It has also been said: ﴿إن صدَّها﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; read: «صدَّها»]: Sulaymān prevented her from what she used to worship; [then] the position of (ما) is accusative, because the verb belongs to Sulaymān. Some of them said: the verb belongs to Allah the Exalted: Allah kept her from what she used to worship.
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ﴾: the alif has kasra, as a new beginning (istiʾnāf). And if a reader read ﴿أنَّها﴾, he would refer it back to the position of (ما) in its nominative: "that she was of a disbelieving people kept her from the worship of Allah". It is like your saying: "What I was engaged in kept me from visiting you — that I was going out early and coming back late": anna explains the meaning of "what I was engaged in".

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿فَرِيقَانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾: the meaning of ﴿يختصمُونَ﴾ is: differing — a believer and a denier.

farraa:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ طَائِرُكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: he says: in the Preserved Tablet with Allah. You take me as an ill omen and augur ill of me, and all of that is from Allah. It is like His saying ﴿قالوا طَائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ﴾, i.e. it is bound to you: whatever there is of good or evil is bound upon your necks. He has made it clear in His saying ﴿وَكُلَّ إنْسَانٍ ألْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ فىعُنُقِهِ﴾.

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ تَقَاسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (تقاسَمُوا بالله), without ﴿قالوا﴾. His saying: ﴿لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ﴾: tāʾ, nūn and yāʾ have all been read. Whoever says ﴿تقاسموا﴾ and makes ﴿تقاسموا﴾ a statement (khabar, i.e. a past verb), it is as though he said "swearing to one another": ﴿لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ﴾ with the nūn. Then the yāʾ is permissible with this meaning, so you say: they said ﴿ليبيتُنَّه﴾ with yāʾ, just as you say lanaqūmanna, layaqūmanna and layaqūmunna. Whoever says taqāsamū and makes it in the position of the jussive [i.e. an imperative], it is as though he said: "Make a pact and swear: you shall surely attack him by night (latubayyitunnahu)" with tāʾ. And the nūn is permissible in this respect, because the one who said to them "swear to one another" is included with them in the act, even though he commanded them; do you not see that you say "Stand up, let us go (nadhhab) to so-and-so", because he commands them while being with them in the act? The nūn is the most pleasing of the options to me. Al-Kisāʾī reads with tāʾ, and the generality [of readers] are on the nūn. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (تقاسَمُوا) (ثم لنُقْسِمَنًّ ما شهِدْنَا مَهْلك أهله). Allah has said ﴿تَعَالَوا نَدْعُ أَبْنَاءَنا وأبْنَاءَكُمْ﴾, because they called them so that all of them should do together what they called them to. The people of Medina, ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan read it with the nūn, and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh with the tāʾ. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna related to me from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj from Mujāhid that he read (ليُبَيِّتُنَّه) with the yāʾ.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ﴾: It is read with kasra, as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), like His saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإنسانُ إلَى طَعَامِهِ أنّا صَبَبْنَا الماءَ﴾: he begins anew while explaining by it what came before. And whoever refers it back to what came before [Translator's note: the source has «على إعلى», a scribal slip for «على»] says (أَنَّا) with fatḥa; then (أَنَّا) is in the position of the nominative, made to follow "the outcome" (al-ʿāqiba). And if you wish, you may make it accusative in two ways: one is to refer it to the position of (كيف); the other is to repeat (كان), as though you said: "the outcome of their plotting was Our destroying them". And if you wish, you may make it a single phrase and put (أَنَّا) in the position of the accusative, as though you said: "so look how the outcome of their plotting was: Our destroying them". And His saying: ﴿وأنتم تبصرونَ تعلمون أَن فاحشة﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently a fragment concerning 27:54].

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿قُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ﴾: It was said to Lūṭ: ﴿قُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ for the destruction of those who were destroyed, ﴿وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ﴾. ﴿ءَآللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: he says: is the worship of Allah better, or the worship of idols?

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَنبَتْنَا بِهِ حَدَآئِقَ ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍ﴾: He said ﴿ذاتَ﴾ and did not say dhawāt, and each is correct. It is permissible to say ﴿ذات﴾ for "gardens", which is a plural, only because you say "these are gardens" just as you say "this is a garden". Similar is the saying of Allah ﴿وَلِلّهِ الأسْمَاءُ الحُسْنَى﴾, where He did not say al-ḥusan, and (والقُرون الأولَي). Had it been "gardens dhawāt bahja", it would be correct. Al-Aʿshā said, using the singular form:
فسوف يُعقبُنيهِ إن ظفرتَ به * ربٌّ غفورٌ وبِيض ذات أطهار
(A forgiving Lord will requite me for it, if you get hold of it, and fair women of purity.)
He did not say dhawāt aṭhār. Ḥadīqa is said only of every orchard that has a wall around it; what has no wall around it is not called ḥadīqa.
His saying: ﴿أَإِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ refers back to His saying ﴿أَمْ مَنْ خَلَق﴾ such-and-such. Then He said ﴿أَإِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ created it? And if you wish, you may make its nominative due to maʿa, as in your saying: "Is there with Allah — woe to you! — a god?" And it could come in the accusative, aʾilāhan maʿa Allāh, by implying a verb through which the accusative arises, as in your saying: "Do you set up a god with Allah?" or "Do you take a god with Allah?"
The Arabs say: "A fox, and you run away?!" (a-thaʿlaban wa-tafirru), as though they meant: "Do you see a fox and run away?" One of the poets said:
أَعبداً حلَّ فى شُعَبىَ غريباً * أَلُؤْماً لا أبالكَ واغترابَا
(A slave settling as a stranger in Shuʿabā? Baseness — may you have no father! — and being a stranger too?)
He means: do you combine baseness and estrangement? I heard one of the Arabs [speak] of a captive he had taken by night; when [138/a] morning came he saw that he was black, and said: "A slave, the whole night through!", as though he said: do I not see that I have captured a slave since my night [began]? Another said:
أجَخْفا تميميّاً إذا فتنة خَبَتْ * وجُبْناً إذا ما المشرفيّة سُلَّت
(Boastfulness, O Tamīmī, when strife has died down, and cowardice when the Mashrafī swords are drawn?)
This is in every [expression of] wonder in which they address the person concerned. But when one wonders at something while addressing someone else, they make the verb govern and say: "A fox, and a man running away from it!" [a-thaʿlabun wa-rajulun yafirru minhu], because this is addressed to someone other than the one with the fox. And if it were put in the accusative according to "Does a man run away from a fox?", you would make the conjoined as though it were the preceding element; it is built on this. I heard one of Banū ʿUqayl recite, by Majnūn of Banū ʿĀmir:
أألبرقَ أم نارا لليلى بدت لنَا * بمُنْخَرقٍ من سَارياتِ الجنائبِ
(Was it lightning, or a fire of Laylā, that appeared to us in a wind-swept tract of the night-travelling south winds?)
And he recited to me in it:
بل البرقَ يبدو فى ذَرَى دَفَئيَّة * يضىء نَشَاصاً مشمخرّ الغَوارب
(Nay, it was lightning appearing in the peaks of a spring cloud, lighting up towering cloud-masses with lofty crests.)
He put all of this in the accusative, with its verb accompanying it, by implying a verb of it, as though he said: do I see a fire? Nay, I see lightning. And as though he said: and if I [only] saw the fire of Laylā. Likewise the other two verses, in His saying ﴿أَإِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿قُل لاَّ يَعْلَمُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاواتِ وٱلأَرْضِ ٱلْغَيْبَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾: You put what comes after (إلاّ) in the nominative because in what precedes it there is a negation (jaḥd), and it [the preceding noun] is nominative. Had it been accusative it would be correct. In one of the two readings: ﴿مَا فعَلوهُ إلا قليلاً منهم﴾ in the accusative, and in our reading in the nominative; each is correct. This is when the negation before illā is with definite nouns. When it is with an indefinite, they say nothing but the following [construction] (itbāʿ) of what precedes (إلاّ); they say: "No one went except your father (abūka)", and they do not say "except abāka". That is because "the father" takes the place of "anyone": this is one and that is one, so they preferred itbāʿ. In the first case, what precedes (إلاَّ) is a plural and what follows (إلاّ) is one of it or part of it, not all of it.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلِ ٱدَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾: its meaning is: perhaps their knowledge has come in succession (tadāraka). He says: their knowledge of the Hereafter followed in succession; he means: with knowledge of the Hereafter, whether it will be or not. That is why He said ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِّنْهَا بَلْ هُم مِّنْهَا عَمُونَ﴾. In the reading of Ubayy: (أَمْ تداركَ عِلمُهُم فى الآخرة) with am. The Arabs put (بل) in place of (أم) and (أم) in place of (بل) when there is an interrogative at the beginning of the speech, as in the poet's saying:
فواالله ما أجرِى أسَلْمَى تَغَوَّلتْ * أم النومُ أم كلّ إلى حَبِيبُ
(By Allah, I do not know: has Salmā changed like a ghoul, or is it sleep, or are all dear to me?)
Their meaning is: bal (nay rather). The readers differed over ﴿ادّارك﴾: Yaḥyā, al-Ḥasan, Shayba and Nāfiʿ read (بل ادَّاركَ); and Mujāhid [and] Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read (بَلْ أَدْرَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِى الآخِرة), from adraktu (I attained), and its meaning is as though he said: has their knowledge attained the knowledge of the Hereafter? It has reached me from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read (بَلَى أَدَّارك), as a question, doubling the dāl and putting a yāʾ in (بلى). That is a good reading, because it is more like mockery of the deniers, as in your saying to a man you are calling a liar: "Yes indeed (balā), by my life, you have met the predecessors, so you relate what we do not relate!" — while you are calling him a liar.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿أَإِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ﴾ and ﴿إنَّنَا﴾: in the copies of the people of Syria it is ﴿إنَّنَا﴾.

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِي تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾: It has come in the exegesis: "some of what you seek to hasten has drawn near to you". It is as though the lām came in because the meaning is "drew near", as the poet said: [138/a]
فقلت لها الحاجَاتُ يطرحن بالفتى * وهمٌّ تعَنّانى مُعَنّىً ركائبُهُ
(I said to her: needs fling a young man about, and a care has wearied me whose mounts are themselves wearied.)
He put the bāʾ on "the young man" because the meaning of ﴿يَطرحن﴾ is "they throw", and you say "I threw [with] the thing (ramaytu bi-l-shayʾ)" and "I flung it". The lām may be intrusive, the meaning being "radifakum" (has followed you), just as some of the Arabs said: "nafadhtu lahā miʾatan", meaning "nafadhtuhā miʾatan" (I paid her a hundred).

farraa:76-76.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ يَقُصُّ عَلَىٰ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ أَكْثَرَ ٱلَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾: That is because the Children of Israel differed until some of them cursed others, so Allah said: this Quran relates to them the guidance concerning what they differed over, if they would take it.

farraa:81-81.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتَ بِهَادِي ٱلْعُمْيِ عَن ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾: Had you said bi-hādin al-ʿumya [with tanwīn and the accusative], it would be correct. Ḥamza read (ومَا أنتَ تَهْدِى العُمْى عَن ضَلاَلتِهم), because in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (وما إن تهدى العمى), which are two negatives combined, as the poet — Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma — said:
ما إن رَأيْتُ ولا سَمعتُ به * كاليوم طالِى أينْقُ جُرْبِ
(I have never seen nor heard of anyone like today's tar-smearer of mangy she-camels.)

farraa:82-82.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا وَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِم﴾: its meaning is: when wrath becomes due upon them. It is like His saying ﴿حَقَّ عليهم القَوْلُ﴾ in another place. His saying ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَآبَّةً مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾: the readers agree on the doubling of ﴿تكلّمهم﴾, and it is from speech (al-kalām). One of the ḥadīth transmitters told me that he said ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾ and ﴿تَكْلِمُهم﴾ ("it will wound them"). His saying (أَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ) is read with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever reads it with fatḥa makes the speaking fall upon it: ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ بأَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾, and its position is accusative. In the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿بأن الناس﴾, and in the reading of Ubayy: (تُنَبِّئهم أنّ الناسَ); these two are evidence for whoever reads it with fatḥa. The people of Medina [read] ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ إِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾, so (إنَّ) is a new statement, yet it carries the meaning of the speech falling [on it]. Similar is ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإنْسانُ إلى طعَامِهِ﴾: whoever says (أَنَّا) makes it genitive, referred back to "food": "to [the fact] that We poured down water"; and whoever reads it with kasra says: innā — He informed [them] of the cause of the food, how Allah decreed it.

farraa:87-87.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ﴾: He did not say fa-yafzaʿu; He made faʿala (the past) refer back to yafʿalu (the imperfect). That is because in meaning it is: "and when the trumpet is blown, then [they] are terrified". Do you not see that your saying "I will stand on the day you stand" is like your saying "I will stand when you stand"? So it was answered with faʿala, because faʿala and yafʿalu are both sound with idhā. If you say: then where is the answer to His saying ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾? I say: it may be in an implied faʿala with the wāw, as though He said: "and that is the day the trumpet is blown". And if you wish, you may say: its answer is left out, as He said ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إذ فَزِعُوا فَلاَ فَوْتَ﴾.
And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ يَرَى الذِينَ ظَلَموا﴾: its answer has been left out. And Allah knows best.
His saying ﴿وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ دَاخِرِينَ﴾: the readers lengthen the alif [ātūhu], meaning: "fāʿilūhu" (coming to Him). Ḥamza shortened it. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: a number of people related to me, among them al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī, Qays and Abū Bakr, all of them from Jaḥsh ibn Ziyād al-Ḍabbī, from Tamīm ibn Ḥadhlam, who said: I recited to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd (وَكُلٌّ آتَوْهُ دَاخِرِينَ) with the alif lengthened, and he said: ﴿وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ﴾ without lengthening the alif. It is a good reading, referred back to His saying ﴿فَفَزِع﴾, as you say in ordinary speech: "he saw me and was terrified, and came back abased". Referring faʿala to its like is more pleasing to me, together with the reading of ʿAbd Allāh. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs related to me from al-Aʿmash from Tamīm from ʿAbd Allāh the like of the report of Abū Bakr and his companions.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ آمِنُونَ﴾: The reading of the readers is with the genitive construct; they said ﴿وَهُمْ مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ [Translator's note: the two forms are identical in the source as printed; the intended contrast is evidently between fazaʿi yawmiʾidhin and yawmaʾidhin]. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read, in a chain of transmission part of which is part of what I related to you: (مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ); Tamīm recited it to them thus: (وَهُمْ من فَزَعٍ يَوْمِئذٍ), and he [Ibn Masʿūd] took it with tanwīn and the accusative. The genitive construct is more pleasing to me — even though I read with the accusative — because it is a known terror; do you not see that He said (لاَ يَحْزُنُهُمْ الفَزَعُ الأَكْبَرُ) and made it [139/a] definite? So annexing it, so that it becomes definite, is more pleasing to me. And it is correct.

farraa:92-92.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنْ أَتْلُوَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ﴾: In one of the two readings: (وَأَنِ اتْلُ), without the wāw, in the jussive as a command. The wāw has been dropped from it because of the jussive as a command, as He said ﴿قُلْ إنّى أُمِرْت أَنْ أَكُون أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ﴾: He made the wāw, with the prohibition, refer back to a word put in the accusative by an, because the meaning comes with (أمرت) in both ways together. Do you not see that you say: "I ordered ʿAbd Allāh that he should stand (an yaqūma)" and "that: stand! (wa-an qum)"? Allah said ﴿وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعَالمينَ وَأَنْ أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاَة﴾, and this is like His saying ﴿وَأَنْ أَتْلُو القرآنَ﴾.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿طس﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has already been given at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.
﴿تلك آيات القرآن وكتاب مبين﴾: تلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject); آيات القرآن is the khabar (predicate); كتاب is conjoined to القرآن; and مبين is a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ألق is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); the speech is conjoined to ﴿بورك﴾; and عصاك is the object. ﴿فلما﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. «فألقاها فاستحالت حية فلما» (so he threw it down, and it turned into a serpent, and when…); ﴿لما﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) meaning "when" (حين), or a linking particle (rābiṭa); رآها is a past verb, with a latent fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿رآها﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) through the adverb's being annexed to it; the clause تهتز is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing here is visual. ﴿كأنها جان﴾: كأن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the hāʾ is its noun (ism), and جان is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of an accusative as a second ḥāl, or it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of تهتز. ﴿ولى﴾ is a past verb, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause ﴿ولى﴾ has no grammatical position; مدبرًا is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of ﴿ولى﴾; the wāw is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; and يعقب is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾.
﴿يا موسى لا تخف إني لا يخاف لدي المرسلون﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted saying that must be supplied, i.e. "He (Exalted is He) said" (قال تعالى); يا is a vocative particle, and ﴿موسى﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun (mufrad ʿalam); لا is prohibitive, and تخف is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾; in ﴿إني﴾, إن is an abrogating particle and the yāʾ is its noun (ism); the clause لا يخاف is its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿إني لا يخاف...﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), giving the reason for the prohibition of fear; ﴿لدي﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخاف﴾; and المرسلون is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿إلا من ظلم ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء﴾: إلا is a particle of exception meaning "but" (لكن); ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun, excepted (mustathnā), in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); or it is a conditional noun that is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is excepted from the most general of states; ظلم is a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿ثم بدل﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ظلم﴾; حسنًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿بعد سوء﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حسنًا﴾.
﴿فإني غفور رحيم﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the response (jawāb) of ﴿من﴾; in ﴿إني﴾, إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and the yāʾ is its noun (ism); and غفور رحيم are its two khabars (predicates).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وأدخل يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿أدخل﴾ is conjoined to ﴿وألق عصاك﴾; يدك is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿في جيبك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أدخل﴾; تخرج is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the imperative, and the fāʿil (agent) of تخرج is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هي); ﴿بيضاء﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of ﴿تخرج﴾; and ﴿من غير سوء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿بيضاء﴾; it has also been said: another ḥāl, or a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿بيضاء﴾.
﴿في تسع آيات إلى فرعون وقومه﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿في تسع آيات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or to an omitted verb, i.e. "go" (اذهب); ﴿إلى فرعون﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted, implied [verb] "go" (اذهب), or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿تسع﴾ or of ﴿آيات﴾; and قومه is conjoined to فرعون.
﴿إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism); the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن; قومًا is the khabar of كانوا, and فاسقين is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause ﴿إنهم﴾ gives the reason for the command to go.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فلما جاءتهم آياتنا مبصرة قالوا هذا سحر مبين﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted; ﴿جاءتهم﴾ is a past verb, the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), آياتنا is the fāʿil (agent), and مبصرة is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿قالوا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿قالوا﴾ has no grammatical position; ﴿هذا﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), سحر is the khabar (predicate), and مبين is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا﴾: جحدوا is conjoined to قالوا; ﴿بها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) جحدوا; the wāw is circumstantial (lil-ḥāl), with ﴿قد﴾ implied after it; استيقنتها أنفسهم is a past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); and ظلمًا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of جحدوا, i.e. "wrongdoing and arrogant" (ظالمين مستكبرين).
﴿فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين﴾: the fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); انظر is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; عاقبة المفسدين is the noun (ism) of كان; and the clause suspends انظر from governing (muʿallaqa), so it is in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), because انظر means "reflect" (تفكر).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ولقد آتينا داود وسليمان علما﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the lām occurs in the response to an implied oath; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); آتينا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); داود is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), سليمان is conjoined to داود, and علمًا is the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وقالا الحمد لله الذي فضلنا على كثير من عباده المؤمنين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and قالا is conjoined to something implied; الحمد is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); الذي is a relative noun, a naʿt (adjective) of الله; the clause فضلنا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. على كثير is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فضلنا; من عباده is a naʿt of كثير; and المؤمنين is a naʿt of عباده.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وورث سليمان داود وقال يا أيها الناس علمنا منطق الطير﴾: the wāw is «ضية» [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently a corrupted word, perhaps for استئنافية (resumptive)]; ورث سليمان داود is a verb, a fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); قال is conjoined to ورث. ﴿يا أيها الناس﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ﴿ها﴾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh); and الناس is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أي﴾. علمنا is a past verb in the passive (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), نا is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and منطق الطير is the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وأوتينا من كل شيء إن هذا لهو الفضل المبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أوتينا is conjoined to علمنا; من كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أوتينا﴾. ﴿إن هذا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and هذا is its noun (ism), this being resumptive speech with no grammatical position; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿هو﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ (subject); الفضل is the khabar (predicate) of إن, or the khabar of هو, the clause [then] being the khabar of إن; and المبين is a naʿt of الفضل.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وحشر لسليمان جنوده من الجن والإنس والطير فهم يوزعون﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); حشر is a past verb in the passive (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu); لسليمان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) حشر; جنوده is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿وحشر لسليمان...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; من الجن والإنس والطير is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جنوده; the fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يوزعون is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿حتى إذا أتوا على واد النمل قالت نملة يا أيها النمل ادخلوا مساكنكم﴾: حتى is a particle of limit (ghāya) for something omitted, its implied form being «فساروا حتى إذا أتوا» (so they marched until, when they came…), or a limit for يوزعون; على وادي النمل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أتوا﴾; the clause قالت نملة has no grammatical position. يا أيها النمل: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ﴿ها﴾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh); and النمل is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أي﴾. ادخلوا مساكنكم is a verb, a fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa).
﴿لا يحطمنكم سليمان وجنوده وهم لا يشعرون﴾: a resumptive prohibition with no connection to what precedes, i.e. "do not be where they would crush you" (لا تكونوا بحيث يحطمونكم); or a badal (substitute) from the imperative clause ﴿ادخلوا مساكنكم﴾. لا is prohibitive; يحطمنكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of a jussive (majzūm) by لا; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); سليمان is the fāʿil (agent), and جنوده is conjoined to سليمان. وهم: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause لا يشعرون is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is circumstantial.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿فتبسم ضاحكا من قولها﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted that the context calls for, i.e. «فسمع قولها المذكور، فتبسم» (so he heard her aforementioned words, and smiled); ضاحكًا is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida, circumstantial); and من قولها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ضاحكًا﴾.
﴿وقال رب أوزعني أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. The clause ﴿قال﴾ is conjoined to تبسم. رب is the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf) to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, and the vocative particle is omitted. أوزعني is a verb of supplication (duʿāʾ), with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), and أن with what falls within its scope is the second object of أوزعني, because it embraces the meaning of inspiring (ilhām); or it is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. «بأن اشكر نعمتك» [Translator's note: so in the source, اشكر, presumably for أشكر (that I give thanks for Your favour)]. ﴿التي﴾ is a relative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a naʿt (adjective) of نعمتك. The clause أنعمت is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. علي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أنعمت, and على والدي is conjoined to علي.
﴿وأدخلني برحمتك في عبادك الصالحين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أدخلني is a verb of supplication (duʿāʾ), a fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); برحمتك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), the bāʾ being causal (lil-sababiyya); في عبادك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أدخلني﴾; and الصالحين is a naʿt (adjective) of عبادك.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿هدى وبشرى للمؤمنين﴾: ﴿هدى﴾ is accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the word governing it being the demonstrative, i.e. "guiding and giving glad tidings" (هادية ومبشرة); or it is nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هي هدى وبشرى» (it is guidance and glad tidings); and ﴿للمؤمنين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿هدى وبشرى﴾.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وتفقد الطير فقال ما لي لا أرى الهدهد أم كان من الغائبين﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿تفقد﴾ is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو), i.e. Solomon, and الطير is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فقال﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تفقد﴾; ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿لا أرى الهدهد﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); أم is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of بل plus the interrogative hamza, the implied form being «بل أكان ...» (rather, was he…?); ﴿كان﴾ is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, and its noun (ism) is a latent pronoun referring back to the hoopoe; and ﴿من الغائبين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of ﴿كان﴾.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿لأعذبنه عذابا شديدا أو لأذبحنه أو ليأتيني بسلطان مبين﴾: the lām occurs in the response to an implied oath; أعذبنه is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "I" (أنا), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عذابا stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), and شديدًا is a naʿt (adjective); أو لأذبحنه is conjoined to لأعذبنه, and أو ليأتيني is likewise conjoined to it; بسلطان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يأتيني﴾; and مبين is a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿فمكث غير بعيد فقال أحطت بما لم تحط به وجئتك من سبأ بنبأ يقين﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); مكث is a past verb, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) referring back to the hoopoe, or to Solomon; the clause ﴿فمكث﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; غير بعيد is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) مكث, or a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted adverb for which it stands in, i.e. "a time not far" (وقتًا غير بعيد) or "a place not far" (مكانًا غير بعيد), in which case it is an adverb of place; فقال is conjoined to مكث; the clause أحطت is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحطت﴾; the clause ﴿لم تحط﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تحط﴾; جئتك is conjoined to أحطت; من سبأ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt of نبأ; بنبأ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جئتك; and يقين is a naʿt of نبأ.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿إني وجدت امرأة تملكهم وأوتيت من كل شيء ولها عرش عظيم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun (ism); the clause وجدت امرأة is the khabar (predicate) of إن; the clause تملكهم is a naʿt (adjective) of امرأة. وأوتيت: the wāw is a conjunction, or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); the clause أوتيت is conjoined to the clause تملكهم, or is circumstantial from the fāʿil (agent) of تملكهم, with ﴿قد﴾ implied; من كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أوتيت﴾, or to an omitted [word] that is the second object of أوتيت, the implied form being «أيضًا من كل شيء» [Translator's note: so in the source; the implied form expected here is probably «شيئًا من كل شيء» (something of everything)]. ﴿لها﴾ is a fronted khabar, عرش is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and عظيم is a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿وجدتها وقومها يسجدون للشمس من دون الله﴾: the clause وجدتها is a badal (substitute) from وجدت امرأة, so it falls within the scope of the khabar (predicate); the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); قومها is conjoined to the hāʾ, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); the clause يسجدون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from its object and what is conjoined to it; للشمس is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسجدون﴾; and من دون الله is a ḥāl.
﴿وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل فهم لا يهتدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; زين is a past verb; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) it; الشيطان is its fāʿil (agent), and أعمالهم is its object; فصدهم is conjoined to زين; عن السبيل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to صدهم. فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause لا يهتدون is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿ألا يسجدوا لله الذي يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض﴾: ألا: ﴿أن﴾ is a maṣdar-forming particle that puts [the verb] in the subjunctive (ḥarf maṣdarī wa-naṣb), and لا is negating or of ṣila (redundant); the interpreted maṣdar ﴿ألا يسجدوا﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the implied form being ﴿فهم لا يهتدون للسجود﴾ (so they are not guided to prostration); or the maṣdar is a badal (substitute) from أعمالهم, the implied form being ﴿وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم عدم السجود﴾ (and Satan made fair-seeming to them their deeds: not prostrating); or the maṣdar is a badal from السبيل. ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسجدوا﴾; الذي is a relative [noun], a naʿt (adjective) of الله; the clause ﴿يخرج﴾ الخبء is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. في السماوات والأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to الخبء, i.e. "what is hidden in the heavens" (المخبوء في السماوات), or to ﴿يخرج﴾, on the view that ﴿في﴾ means "from" (من), i.e. "He brings it out from the heavens and the earth" (يخرجه من السماوات والأرض).
﴿ويعلم ما تخفون وما تعلنون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يعلم is conjoined to يخرج, so it falls within the scope of the ṣila (relative clause); the fāʿil (agent) of يعلم is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring back to Allah; ما is a relative [noun], the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause تخفون is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ما تعلنون is conjoined to ما تخفون.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿الله﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation (nāfiya lil-jins).
﴿إله﴾: its noun (ism), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of لا together with its noun, because their position is nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ; or a badal from the pronoun latent (mustakinn) in the omitted khabar (predicate). The clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is the khabar of ﴿الله﴾.
﴿رب العرش العظيم﴾: ﴿رب﴾ is a badal from ﴿هو﴾; العرش is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿العظيم﴾ is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿قال سننظر أصدقت أم كنت من الكاذبين﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; قال is a past verb, and the clause سننظر is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the hamza is for interrogation; صدقت is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); أم is connective (muttaṣila), counterbalancing the hamza (muʿādila lil-hamza); in ﴿كنت﴾, كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun (ism); and ﴿من الكاذبين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون﴾: اذهب is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); بكتابي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) اذهب; هذا is a naʿt (adjective) of كتابي, or a badal (substitute) from it. فألقه: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ألقه is an imperative verb, with a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ألقه﴾; ثم is a conjunction; تول is an imperative verb, [indeclinable] on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت); عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); فانظر is conjoined to تول; ماذا is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a fronted object of يرجعون; or ما is an interrogative noun that is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and ذا is a relative noun meaning الذي, the khabar (predicate) of ما, and the clause يرجعون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿قالت يا أيها الملأ إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun (ism); the clause ألقي is its khabar (predicate); إلي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ألقي﴾; كتاب is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and كريم is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون﴾: الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of المؤمنين, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who" (هم الذين); the clause ﴿يقيمون الصلاة﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, a clause with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿يؤتون الزكاة﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يقيمون الصلاة﴾. ﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (lil-ḥāl), or a conjunction (lil-ʿaṭf); ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ; ﴿بالآخرة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يوقنون﴾; ﴿هم﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); يوقنون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause يوقنون is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun (ism); من سليمان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of إن. وإنه: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; the clause of the basmala is its khabar; بسم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted, the bāʾ being for seeking help (lil-istiʿāna) or for adhesion (lil-ilṣāq); the implied form of the omitted word is "I begin" (أبتدئ), so the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); or "my beginning" (ابتدائي), so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and الرحمن الرحيم are two naʿts (adjectives) of Allah.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿إن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة زينا لهم أعمالهم﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الذين is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the noun (ism) of إن; لا is negating; يؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause لا يؤمنون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿بالآخرة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمنون﴾; زين is a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿زينا﴾; ﴿أعمالهم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause ﴿زينا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن.
﴿فهم يعمهون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يعمهون is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿أولئك الذين لهم سوء العذاب﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and الذين is its khabar (predicate); ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar, and سوء العذاب is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause ﴿لهم سوء العذاب﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون﴾: ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿في الآخرة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿الأخسرون﴾; الأخسرون is its khabar (predicate); ﴿هم﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); and الأخسرون is the khabar. [Translator's note: the source names الأخسرون as the khabar twice; translated as written.]

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وإنك لتلقى القرآن من لدن حكيم عليم﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its noun (ism); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿تلقى﴾ is an imperfect verb in the passive (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); the clause تلقى is its khabar (predicate); القرآن is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من لدن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تلقى﴾; حكيم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and عليم is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿إذ قال موسى لأهله إني آنست نارا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, the implied form being «اذكر إذ قال موسى» (remember when Moses said); ﴿قال﴾ is a past verb, and موسى is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿لأهله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾. ﴿إني آنست نارًا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun (ism); آنست is a past verb, the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and نارا is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause آنست is the khabar (predicate) of إن; and the clause ﴿إني آنست نارًا﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿سآتيكم منها بخبر أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; آتيكم is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I" (أنا), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿منها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿خبر﴾; ﴿بخبر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿آتيكم﴾; ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction; آتيكم is conjoined to the first آتيكم; ﴿بشهاب﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to آتيكم; قبس is a badal (substitute) from شهاب, or a naʿt of it on its being interpreted as a passive participle, i.e. «شهاب مقتبس من نار» (a brand taken from a fire). ﴿لعلكم تصطلون﴾: لعل is an abrogating particle, and the kāf is its noun (ism); the clause ﴿تصطلون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of لعل; and the clause ﴿لعلكم تصطلون﴾ is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), i.e. "hoping to secure warmth for you and provide it" (راجيًا تأمين الدفء لكم وتوفيره).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted for brevity; لما is temporal (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya, "when"), or a linking particle (rābiṭa); جاءها is a past verb, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿نودي﴾ is a past verb in the passive (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu); the clause ﴿نودي﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of ﴿نودي﴾ is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو), referring back to Moses. ﴿أن﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), because the calling carries the sense of saying; ﴿بورك﴾ is a past verb in the passive, and ﴿مَن﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿في النار﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [word] that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿من حولها﴾ is conjoined to ﴿من في النار﴾; and the clause ﴿بورك﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), having entered upon the past verb, and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن بورك﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the clause ﴿بورك﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿وسبحان الله رب العالمين﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; سبحان stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb; the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and رب العالمين is a badal (substitute) or a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يا موسى إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم﴾: يا is a vocative particle, and موسى is the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun (mufrad ʿalam); in ﴿إنه﴾, إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and the hāʾ is its noun (ism); أنا is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿الله﴾ is the khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of إن; and العزيز الحكيم are two naʿts (adjectives).

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: فَلَمَّا جاءَ سُلَيْمانَ قالَ أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمالٍ: if you wish, you may assimilate (idghām) the nūn into the nūn, and that is permissible, even though it involves bringing two quiescent letters together.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ بِجُنُودٍ لا قِبَلَ لَهُمْ بِها: a lām of oath, and the nūn is necessarily attached to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān say: it is a lām of emphasis (tawkīd); and likewise his view was that the lāms are all three and no more: the lām of emphasis, the lām of command, and the lām of the genitive (khafḍ). This is the view of the most skilled grammarians, because they return a thing to its origin, and this is only possible for one who is well practised in Arabic. أَذِلَّةً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَهُمْ صاغِرُونَ: also in the position of a ḥāl.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: It was said: what he meant by this is that if they came as Muslims (in submission), it would not be permissible to bring her throne except with her permission. And it was said: what Solomon ﷺ intended was to display a miraculous sign.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
قالَ عِفْرِيتٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ: Abū Isḥāq said: the ʿifrīt is the one who is effective in affairs and goes to extremes in them, who has malice and cunning. One also says: ʿifr, ʿifāriya and ʿifriya. It is reported from Abū Rajāʾ that he read: قال عفرية من الجنّ. One also says: ʿifriya nifriya, as an itbāʿ (rhyming echo-pairing). Whoever says ʿifriya forms its plural as ʿafārin; and whoever says
ʿifrīt has three options in the plural: if he wishes he says ʿafārīt; if he wishes he says ʿafārin, because the tāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), just as one says ṭawāghin as the plural of ṭāghūt; and if he wishes he compensates for the tāʾ and says:
ʿafāriyy.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is: that He may see whether I give thanks or am ungrateful. Someone else said: the meaning of «ليبلوني» is «to make me His servant in worship», and it is figurative (majāz).

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: قالَ نَكِّرُوا لَها عَرْشَها: al-Farrāʾ claimed that he only ordered it to be disguised because the devils had told him: there is something wrong in her mind; so he wanted to test her. نَنْظُرْ: jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the command; and whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a new, resumptive clause. أَتَهْتَدِي: there are two views on its meaning. One of them: will she be guided to recognising it; and the other: will she be guided by this great sign and know that none brings it except a prophet from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and so be guided and abandon error.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t:
قالَتْ كَأَنَّهُ هُوَ: the khabar (predicate) of kaʾanna is referred to by a pronoun, because it has already been mentioned. وَأُوتِينَا الْعِلْمَ مِنْ قَبْلِها: it was said:
the knowledge of tawḥīd (the Oneness of Allah). وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ: it was said: because her people had become Muslims before her.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
«ما» may be in the position of the nominative, i.e. her worship apart from Allah and her worship of it prevented her from knowing what we have known, from submitting [Translator's note: so in the text: «عن أن تعلم ما علمناه عن أن تسلم»]. And «ما» may be in the position of the accusative, the implied meaning being: and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prevented her from her worship — i.e. and Solomon ﷺ prevented her from her worship — so «عن» was omitted and the verb became transitive. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 321-
ونبئت عبد الله بالجوّ أصبحت ... كراما مواليها لئيما صميمها
(I was told that ʿAbd Allāh in al-Jaww came to have noble clients while its pure stock was base.)
And he claimed that in his view the meaning is «I was told about ʿAbd Allāh». Whoever reads (أنّها) with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa, anna is in the position of the accusative in the sense of «because she»; and it may be a badal (substitute) for «ما». The kasra is on the basis of a new (resumptive) clause.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
[Translator's note: the opening words of the quotation are cut off in the text: «لَ لَهَا» for قِيلَ لَهَا.] لَ لَهَا ادْخُلِي الصَّرْحَ
The implied form according to the doctrine of Sībawayh is «ادخلي إلى الصرح»; «إلى» was omitted and the verb was made transitive. Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] judges him to be in error in this; he said: because «دخل» indicates an object.
[Translator's note: likewise cut off: «لَتْ» for قَالَتْ.] لَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي
Inna is given kasra because it is at the start of a clause after the verb of saying; and some Arabs give it fatḥa, making the verb of saying govern it. أَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمانَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ
If you make [the ʿayn of] «عَ» [i.e. مع] quiescent [Translator's note: the word is truncated in the text as «عَ»],
it is a particle that has come for a meaning, without disagreement among the grammarians. If you give it fatḥa, there are two views: one of them is that it is a noun in the sense of an adverb (ẓarf), and the other that it is a genitive-governing particle, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا إِلى ثَمُودَ أَخاهُمْ صالِحاً: it is made a name for the tribe and so is treated as a diptote (not inflected with tanwīn); inflecting it fully is good, taking it as a name for the clan. فَإِذا هُمْ فَرِيقانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ: according to the meaning; and «يختصمان» would be according to the wording.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: قالَ يا قَوْمِ لِمَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. why did you say: «If what you have brought is true, then bring us the punishment».

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: قالُوا اطَّيَّرْنا بِكَ وَبِمَنْ مَعَكَ: Mujāhid said: i.e. we have taken an evil omen. Abū Isḥāq said: the origin is «تطيّرنا»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ because it is from its place of articulation, and the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was brought in so as not to begin with a quiescent letter; when you join it [to what precedes], you drop it. قالَ طائِرُكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ: al-Farrāʾ said: he is saying: in the Preserved Tablet with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is [the cause of] your taking me as an evil omen and your augury; and that is from Allah the Exalted — like His saying طائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ [Yā Sīn: 19], i.e. whatever good or evil there is clings to you; it clings to you and is around your necks.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t:
وَكانَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ: [رهط] is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); its plural is arhuṭ, and the plural of the plural is arāhiṭ.
يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا يُصْلِحُونَ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: these nine were the great men of the people of the city. They used to cause corruption and command corruption. They sat beneath a huge rock by a river, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, overturned it upon them and killed them; «so those are their houses, empty because of the wrong they did».

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: قالُوا تَقاسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ وَأَهْلَهُ: this is among the best readings of this word, because those addressed are included in it in both wording and meaning. And if one reads «لتبيّننّه» [Translator's note: so in the text, apparently for «لتبيّتنّه», the second-person reading], those addressed are not included in the wording but are included in the meaning. The reading of Mujāhid is «ليبيّتنّه» with yāʾ. Abū Isḥāq said: لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ, i.e. they said «we shall surely attack him by night» while swearing to one another, i.e. making mutual oaths. ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِ ما شَهِدْنا مَهْلِكَ أَهْلِهِ: «مهلك» is in the sense of «destruction» (ihlāk), and it can be in the sense of an adverb (ẓarf). From ʿĀṣim: «ما شهدنا مهتل» [Translator's note: so in the text; probably «مَهْلَك» (mahlak) is intended], in the sense of «perishing» (halāk); and also from him مَهْلِكَ, which is a noun of the place of perishing, as you say: majlis.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: وَمَكَرُوا مَكْراً: i.e. what they did. وَمَكَرْنا مَكْراً: We requited them for that. And it was said: plotting (makr) on the part of Allah is bringing the deserved punishment from where the servant does not realise.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ: the Kufans, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read — and it is the reading of al-Kisāʾī — أَنَّا دَمَّرْناهُمْ with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that its fatḥa comes from two directions: one of them is that you refer it back to «كيف». Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not hold, because «كيف» is interrogative and «أنّا» is not included in the interrogative.
